sections.h2: Which selling route suits a Macon owner?
sections.html:
Macon owners have three routes: an agent listing, a sale handled by the owner, or a purchase by a cash buyer. Weigh repair needs against the date you need funds.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the best price when the house shows well, with the longest timeline and the most preparation.
  • Selling on your own: keeps the agent's share of the price, while showings, contracts and buyer questions land on you.
  • Cash sale as-is: suits vacant, inherited, tax-delinquent or storm-worn houses, where repairs would cost more than the discount you give up.

With no mortgage involved, there is no lender appraisal to wait on. That helps when a house carries deferred repairs that an appraiser would flag.

Macon is governed as Macon-Bibb County, a single consolidated government, so most local figures are county figures. The 2025 estimate is 157,556 residents, almost level with the 157,346 counted in April 2020. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $174,500, 51.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,066 a month.

At that price level, repair costs take a larger bite out of a sale than they would in a pricier market. Check any offer against sales close to your address, because one block can price very differently from the next.

Macon's older core affects what owners may do to a building. County Planning and Zoning has been updating design guidelines for the central business districts and the historic districts, including Intown, the Central Business District, Vineville and Cherokee Heights. Those guidelines cover exterior changes, new construction and demolitions.

If your house sits inside one of those districts, ask Macon-Bibb Planning and Zoning what review applies before you promise a buyer anything about exterior work, and before you agree to a repair credit that involves siding, windows or porches.

sections.h2: Vacant or run-down houses and blight rules
sections.html:
The county takes abandoned and unsafe buildings seriously, and a vacant house left alone can pick up tax consequences or a demolition order. Under the county's blight program, a property counts as blight when it meets at least two listed criteria, such as being uninhabitable or abandoned, having severely overgrown vegetation at 12 inches or higher, or failing to meet code for at least one year after written notice.

An unkempt yard alone is not blight, and loose animals and abandoned vehicles go to other offices. For a property reported as blighted, the Office of the Mayor may send a "nuisance per se" letter, and the owner may then repair or demolish the structure. If the owner does neither, the county may proceed with demolition.

In the blight tax process the property must be vacant and the owner may appeal the designation. Properties not appealed can be placed on a list sent to the Tax Commissioner each August. Code Enforcement takes reports and completion notices at 478-803-0470.

An heir holding an empty house should deal with any notice early. Buyers who pay cash often reflect an open notice in the price instead of walking away.

Each spring the Macon-Bibb Board of Tax Assessors mails the owner of record a notice of assessment, as state law requires. The notice carries a 45-day window for a written appeal. The letter must name the appeal route you choose, and it must be hand delivered or mailed with a dated postmark, because emails and faxes are not accepted.

Appeal routes after a Bibb County notice of assessment
RouteWhat it coversCost
Board of EqualizationAny property; grounds limited to value or uniformityNo cost unless an agent is hired
Hearing officerNon-homesteaded real property and large wireless personal propertyNo cost unless an agent is hired
Nonbinding arbitrationReal property valuation only; owner supplies a certified appraisalThe party farthest from the final value pays the arbitrator

Either side may take a Board of Equalization decision to superior court within 30 days.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and who to call
sections.html:
The county's September 2025 resolution puts the residential homestead exemption at $7,000. Officials also asked the local legislative delegation for added exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85. A new local exemption needs a local act and a ballot vote, so ask the Board of Assessors whether the senior tiers are in effect before you count on them.

The Board is at 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, phone 478-200-5550. The Tax Commissioner is at 610 Mulberry Street, phone 478-621-6500. Before fixing a closing date, call the Tax Commissioner for the live bill and any balance owed.

sections.h2: Georgia transfer tax on a Macon sale
sections.html:
Georgia taxes the transfer of title itself, and the Bibb clerk will not record the deed until payment is made. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 (or fractional part of $1,000), then 10 cents per extra $100 (or fractional part of $100).

By statute, O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10, the seller is liable, though sales contracts often shift payment to the buyer. Sellers complete a PT-61 form online through the state clerks' authority. Exemption questions go to the Bibb County clerk's office.

sections.h2: From first offer to closing day
sections.html:
1. Settle or disclose any county notice about the building.
  2. Call the Tax Commissioner for the live bill and any balance, then give that figure to the closing attorney.
  3. Decide in writing whether you or the buyer pays the state transfer tax.
  4. Have the PT-61 filed and the deed delivered to the Bibb clerk for recording.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the repair demands that often follow one. A listing gives you the widest pool of buyers, but the buyer's financing sets the closing date. In either case, an open code notice or an unpaid tax balance is easier to fix before the offer than after it.

Pull together the deed, your latest assessment notice and tax bill, any code or blight letters, and mortgage payoff details. Add a list of repairs you already know about, so a buyer hears them from you first. Having these ready speeds up a cash offer and keeps a listed sale from stalling at closing.

faqs.q: Is a vacant Macon house with code problems still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes, though settle or disclose any county notice first. If Code Enforcement flagged blight, follow the letter and report completion at 478-803-0470, or tell the buyer about the open notice up front. Some cash buyers take the house with the notice open and adjust their price.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Bibb County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date, and the appeal must be on paper. Hand deliver the letter or mail it with a dated postmark, since email and fax are not accepted. Name your chosen route in the letter.

faqs.q: Does Macon-Bibb County offer a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, a $7,000 exemption on a residential homestead. The county also asked state legislators for extra exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85, which need a local act and a ballot vote, so ask the Board of Assessors what applies to you.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a Macon closing?
faqs.a: By statute the seller owes it, though the sales contract can hand the cost to the buyer. Read your contract, and ask the Bibb clerk about any exemption that might fit.

faqs.q: What documents should I gather before selling a Macon house?
faqs.a: Collect the deed, your latest assessment notice and tax bill, any code or blight letters, and mortgage payoff details. Add a list of repairs you know about.
